newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Q1 steel output rose 10 pct -industry group.
newsitem.headline: German Q1 steel output rose 10 pct -industry group.

text.p: German steel production rose 10 percent in the first quarter of 1997, while orders increased 15 percent, the Wirtschaftsvereinigung Stahl, a steel industry associaion, said on Monday.
Steel prices were also starting to rise after a 10 percent decline in 1996, the group's president Ruprecht Vondran, told journalists at the Hanover Industry Trade Fair.
"Steel demand is holding at a good level. We expect that it will rise in the next few months," he said.
German crude steel output should rise six percent in 1997 to 42 million tonnes, and steel makers' profits should also improve, with all steel makers in the black. Some showed losses in 1996, he said.
The 15 percent decline in the mark versus the dollar has boosted steel as well as other German exporters, Vondran said.
While the current market is improving, German steel producers still face structural problems, as shown by the recent merger of the flat-steel operations of Thyssen AG and Krupp, he said.

Production will increasingly be focused in locations with the best logistics and the lowest costs, but Germany will retain basic production capacities even in the low-tech, crude steel end of the market, he said.
The Thyssen-Krupp merger will help to reduce overcapacity, and focus new investments in a less redundant way.
-- Terence Gallagher, Hanover Trade Fair Newsroom
